newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: Former wartime foes square off in El Salvador vote.
newsitem.headline: Former wartime foes square off in El Salvador vote.

text.p: Two former wartime foes square off in key elections in El Salvador on Sunday in a test of democracy for this Central American nation.

Recent polls show the former guerrillas of the left-wing Farabundo Marti Liberation Movement (FMLN) ahead of the ruling right-wing National Republican Alliance (ARENA) in the race to capture the Congress and 262 mayoral seats.

The two sides were locked in a stalemate on the battlefield a little more than five years ago, and now the leftist former guerrillas appear poised to at least pull even with the ruling party once again. ARENA humbled the FMLN in their first electoral challenge three years ago.

"It is possible that we will see a change in the balance of power in the Legislative Assembly and it is possible that the opposition will take a few mayor's posts from the ARENA," Rodolfo Cardenal, vice-dean of the Universidad Centroamericana (Central American University), told Reuters.
Some 2.6 million voters will choose among 13 parties to fill positions for 84 deputies in Congress and for 262 mayors, according the Supreme Electoral Tribunal.
Various opinion polls have signalled a decline in fortunes for ARENA and an increase in support for the FMLN, putting that party slightly ahead in voter intentions.

Analysts said that support has waned for ARENA, drained and weary after being in power since 1989, and voters will use the chance to punish the government. Internal divisions between ARENA hardliners and moderates also wounded the party.

But ARENA has been stirring up fear of the FMLN, reminding voters of hidden arms and atrocities committed during the 12-year civil war that ended with a peace treaty in January 1992. Some 75,000 Salvadorans died in the war.

Officials of ARENA, among them President Armando Calderon Sol, are confident that the party will retain its superiority in the Congress, where it now holds 39 seats. The FMLN seeks to improve on its 20 seats.
Calderon Sol said he believed ARENA would also gain a majority of the municipal councils in the country of 5.8 million people, most of whom live in grinding poverty.
Some observers have severely criticised the parties for mud-slinging and insults during the campaign.
The nature of the campaign "fills us with worries rather than with hope," said Gregorio Rosa Chavez, the assistant bishop for San Salvador.
While for the most part the parties used popular songs to get across their campaign themes, ARENA used its party hymn with the lyrics, "El Salvador will be the tomb where the leftists end up."
Roman Catholic Church officials have warned about electoral fraud, but Calderon Sol has rejected the possibility.
Opposition parties have organised surveillance, with about 1,000 observers from various countries taking part.
The opposition parties have also met with the Defence Minister, Gen. Jaime Guzman, who promised that the military would remain neutral in the elections.
The National Civil Police plans to mobilise more than 10,000 agents to guarantee security during the vote.
